metadata.project: Detecting AI-Generated Images via Physical Sensor Noise and Frequency Domain Forensics
metadata.supervisor: Dr. Tony Scanlan, University of Limerick

ablation_study.note: Seven ablation variants evaluated. v4 adds Z-normalisation (std floor 0.01). v5/v5b adds ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 backbone. v5b is the definitive best (50 epochs).

F1_only_PRNU.note: AUC=0.5 — PRNU stream with random encoder fails to learn

F2_F3_v1.note: v1: NSS passed raw (18-dim) to FusionHead

F2_F3_v2_NSSEncoder_fixed.note: v2: NSSEncoder (18->64 dim projection) added, +4.9pp AUC

F2_F3_v3_seed_fixed.note: v3: encoder seed fixed to 0; comparable to v2

F2_F3_v4_normalised.note: v4: Z-normalisation (std floor 0.01) applied — +12.7pp AUC over v3
F2_F3_v4_normalised.limitation: Random ResNet-18 init — AUC≈0.5 on fresh images (encoder mismatch)

F2_F3_v5_pretrained_20epochs.note: v5: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 backbone, 20 epochs — +3.9pp AUC over v4

F2_F3_v5b_pretrained_50epochs.note: v5b: pretrained backbone, 50 epochs — +5.4pp AUC over v4, BEST VARIANT

F1_F2_F3_v3.note: v3: 500 samples/class, unnormalised — poor due to small subset

F1_F2_F3_v4_normalised.note: v4: normalised; PRNU stream reduces AUC vs F2+F3 alone (0.739 vs 0.865)

key_findings: PRNU stream (F1) consistently degrades performance: AUC=0.500 alone, reduces F2+F3 by -7.2pp
NSS (F3) outperforms FFT (F2) alone: 0.624 vs 0.603 AUC
F2+F3 fusion improves over either stream alone: 0.640 vs 0.624/0.603
Feature Z-normalisation (std floor 0.01) is the largest single improvement: +12.7pp AUC (0.686->0.811)
NSSEncoder projection (18->64 dim) adds +4.9pp over raw NSS features
ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 backbone (+5.4pp AUC, 0.811->0.865) and fixes generalisation: AUC 0.5->0.91 on fresh images
Longer training (50 vs 20 epochs) adds +1.5pp AUC with pretrained backbone (0.850->0.865)

per_generator_breakdown.evaluation_method: Fresh image extraction using saved stream2_encoder.pth + nss_encoder.pth from features_combined; threshold=0.1723 (Youden's J)
per_generator_breakdown.note: Per-generator AUC is NaN because each generator subset has a single class; overall AUC=0.919 computed across all 1500 samples

real.note: 82.4% correctly classified as real (17.6% false positive rate at threshold=0.1723)

stable_diffusion.note: 78.4% of SD1.5 images correctly detected as fake — matches Youden TPR=0.7819

stylegan3.note: 93.0% of StyleGAN3 images correctly detected — GAN spectral artifacts strongly captured

v5b_comparison.note: StyleGAN3 slightly lower due to lower threshold (0.1723 vs v5b 0.2342), but SD and real both improved

generalization_analysis.finding: v5b with pretrained ResNet-18 achieves AUC=0.9107 on 1500 fresh images never seen during training — the generalisation failure of v4 is fully resolved
generalization_analysis.v4_root_cause: Random ResNet-18 initialisation produced image-distribution-specific noise projections. FusionHead memorised patterns from training subset that did not generalise.
generalization_analysis.v5b_fix: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 backbone (layers 2+) produces semantically consistent spectral feature representations regardless of which images are processed. Only the 1-channel conv1 remains randomly initialised (required for single-channel spectral input).
generalization_analysis.evidence: v4: fresh image mean feature deviation +28.8% from training distribution. v5b: fresh image extraction AUC=0.9107 (higher than in-distribution test AUC=0.8651, likely due to full-range class separation in per-generator eval).
generalization_analysis.recommendation: Pretrained backbone is essential for deployment. Future work: fine-tune the backbone end-to-end rather than frozen, and evaluate on ForenSynths/DiffusionForensics benchmarks.

v4_proxy.method: Session 3 proxy evaluation with fresh classifier (200+200 images, 15 epochs, unnormalised)
v4_proxy.note: Proxy method — relative sensitivity only, not absolute performance
v4_proxy.key_finding: Gaussian blur most harmful (sigma=4: ΔAUC=-0.034). JPEG minimal. Resize negligible.

v5b_sweep.method: Direct evaluation on 200 real + 200 fake fresh images with the trained v5b model + pretrained ResNet-18 encoder
v5b_sweep.note: True robustness of the trained model (not proxy). Baseline AUC=0.874 on clean fresh images.
key_findings: JPEG compression is highly robust: even Q=30 causes only ΔAUC=-0.005 from 0.874 baseline
Gaussian blur is the most harmful perturbation: sigma=4 causes ΔAUC=-0.237 (AUC 0.874→0.637)
Bicubic downscale (0.5x) causes ΔAUC=-0.051; upscale (1.5x) negligible at -0.010
Pretrained backbone is 7× more blur-sensitive than v4 random init (ΔAUC -0.237 vs -0.034), likely because ImageNet texture features rely on high-frequency information destroyed by blur
JPEG robustness is similar to v4 (both ~ΔAUC=-0.005 at Q=30), suggesting this is a property of FFT spectral features rather than the backbone

baseline_comparisons.note: Comparison against published baselines. Our model evaluated on COCO+SD+StyleGAN3, not identical benchmarks — comparison is indicative.
baseline_comparisons.assessment: Our v5b model (AUC=0.865 in-distribution, AUC=0.911 fresh-image) is competitive with published baselines on the training-distribution generators. Cross-generator evaluation on ForenSynths/DiffusionForensics is the next step; these datasets require HuggingFace authentication.

cross_benchmark_evaluation.note: Model trained on COCO real + SD1.5/StyleGAN3 fake. Evaluated on 21 unseen generator types from CNNSpot-small (200 real + 200 fake per generator where both classes present).

overall.note: Includes imagenet/laion real-only buckets in ACC; AUC computed over all labelled pairs

key_findings: Overall cross-generator AUC=0.566 — above random (0.5), better than Cozzolino 2024 cross-generator ACC ~38%
CycleGAN: AUC=0.707 — best detected; translation-based GAN produces strong frequency artifacts
LDM variants (diffusion): AUC=0.638-0.660 — decent detection, similar artifact space to training (SD1.5)
DALL-E: AUC=0.610 — transfers reasonably to commercial diffusion model
StyleGAN/StyleGAN2: AUC=0.552-0.613 — related to training generator (StyleGAN3), transfers partially
Deepfake (face swap): AUC=0.477 — below random; fundamentally different artifact type, model has no signal
ProGAN/BigGAN/CRN: AUC=0.510-0.519 — near-random; older GANs not represented in training distribution
Pattern: model generalises to diffusion/LDM generators better than older GAN architectures
Gap vs in-distribution: AUC drops from 0.865 (in-dist) to 0.566 (cross-generator) — 30pp gap
Compared to Cozzolino 2024 baseline (~38% cross-generator ACC): our ACC=55.3% is 17pp better
Overall cross-generator AUC=0.537 on ForenSynths (13 GAN architectures, all unseen during training)
WhichFaceIsReal best: AUC=0.604 -- facial GAN artifacts partially detected by FFT features
StyleGAN2 second: AUC=0.588 -- related to training generator (StyleGAN3), partial transfer
ProGAN near-random: AUC=0.507 -- older GAN architecture not in training distribution
SeeingDark worst: AUC=0.496 (below random) -- dark/HDR photography with camera-specific artifacts confuses detector
ForenSynths overall AUC=0.537 vs CNNSpot-small AUC=0.555 -- comparable cross-benchmark generalization
Both benchmarks show ~5-6pp above random (0.5) -- model has weak but real cross-generator signal
Pattern: model generalizes slightly better to face/texture GANs (StyleGAN2, WhichFaceIsReal) than older class-conditional GANs (ProGAN, BigGAN)

cnnspot_balanced.key_finding: Balanced sampling improves cross-benchmark generalization by +1.1pp AUC

vs_combined_forensynths.note: Marginal improvement; balanced sampling does not significantly change ForenSynths cross-gen generalisation

key_findings: Balanced model ForenSynths overall AUC=0.539 vs combined AUC=0.537 — +0.18pp, effectively identical
WhichFaceIsReal best: AUC=0.602 (consistent across both models)
StyleGAN2 second: AUC=0.586 (related to training generator StyleGAN3)
IMLE notable improvement: AUC=0.548->0.581 (+2.6pp, balanced threshold better calibrated)
CycleGAN: AUC=0.549->0.565 (+1.6pp with balanced threshold)
SeeingDark worst: AUC=0.500 (random chance — HDR photography confuses detector)
StarGAN: AUC=0.500 — balanced model no help for face-attribute transfer GAN
Threshold change 0.172->0.5 shifts TPR/TNR trade-off but AUC is threshold-independent
ForenSynths AUC consistent with CNNSpot-small (0.566): ~5-6pp above random across benchmarks

vs_v5b_subset_comparison.key_insight: Training on 8x more data with 79% real / 21% fake imbalance shifts the model threshold. AUC (threshold-free) is essentially unchanged for in-distribution data (+0.7pp for fresh images). To exploit both: use this model with a calibrated lower threshold (~0.35) for deployment, or retrain with class weighting.

robustness_sweep.method: 200 real + 200 fake fresh images sampled from full dataset (random.seed(123))
key_findings: JPEG robustness: excellent, Q=30 causes only ΔAUC=-0.004 (same as v5b — property of spectral features)
Gaussian blur: sigma=4 ΔAUC=-0.375 (v5b was -0.237); higher absolute drop from higher baseline (0.897→0.522)
Blur absolute floor: ~0.52 AUC at sigma=4 (similar to v5b 0.637 — both drop to near-random)
Bicubic resize: more robust than v5b (0.5x drop: -0.037 vs -0.051); more data may help spatial stability
Baseline clean AUC=0.897 > v5b AUC=0.874 on fresh 400 images (+2.3pp discrimination improvement)

real_bucket_acc.explanation: Full model correctly rejects 87-88% of CNNSpot real images as real, vs only 57-63% for v5b. Class imbalance shifts threshold.

key_findings: Overall cross-generator AUC=0.550 — slightly lower than v5b (0.566), same above-random pattern
CycleGAN: AUC=0.701 — still best detected (consistent across both models)
Deepfake: AUC=0.541 — improved from below-random (v5b=0.477) to above-random
DALL-E: AUC=0.655 — improved from v5b (0.610); commercial diffusion better detected
GLIDE variants: AUC=0.430-0.460 — degraded from v5b; class imbalance may hurt early LDM models
Real-bucket accuracy: 87-88% (vs v5b 57-63%) — model strongly calibrated for COCO-like real images
Vs Cozzolino 2024 baseline (~38% ACC): full model ACC=53.2% is still +15pp better
8x more data did not improve cross-generator AUC; likely needs class weighting or balanced resampling

prnu_validation.method: PRNU NCC discriminability test — Pearson correlation between RAISE-1k D7000 TIFF fingerprint (10 images, 256x256 centre-crop) and DnCNN noise residuals of 100 real COCO + 100 fake SD1.5 + 50 fake StyleGAN3
prnu_validation.finding: AUC=0.379 — below random, direction reversed. Fake images (especially StyleGAN3, mean NCC=0.311) correlate MORE with the D7000 fingerprint than real COCO images (mean NCC=0.183). This is the opposite of PRNU theory expectations.

explanation.real_images: COCO images come from diverse internet cameras (not D7000) — low, variable NCC with D7000 fingerprint (expected).
explanation.stylegan3_anomaly: StyleGAN3 has highest NCC (0.311 > 0.183 real). StyleGAN3 structured spectral patterns spuriously correlate with camera fingerprint extracted via DnCNN. DnCNN trained on Gaussian noise does not correctly isolate camera PRNU from GAN spectral artifacts.
explanation.dncnn_limitation: DnCNN was trained for blind Gaussian denoising, not PRNU extraction. Its 'noise residuals' for GAN images capture GAN-specific periodic artifacts rather than true sensor noise, causing reversed correlation.
explanation.cross_camera_problem: PRNU theory requires test images to come from the same camera as the reference fingerprint. COCO test images do not come from D7000 cameras — the method is inapplicable without per-camera reference images.

prnu_validation.thesis_significance: This empirically validates the decision to exclude the PRNU stream (F1) from the best model. The ablation finding (F1 alone: AUC=0.500; F1+F2: AUC=0.599 vs F2 alone: 0.603; F1+F3: 0.620 vs F3 alone: 0.624) is now explained by the NCC test: PRNU features carry anti-correlated noise that the fusion head cannot usefully exploit. Stream 1 is correctly excluded from the final architecture.
prnu_validation.recommendation: DO NOT add Stream 1 to production model. Document as a validated negative result with mechanistic explanation for thesis.
